Q: Customising scale bar colours in rayshader to match map palette A:

Skip creating the legend using render_scalebar(). Instead, we can save the snapshot to a file, create the legend using {ggplot2} and then overlay it on top of the final image;

render_snapshot("scene.png", clear = TRUE)

library(ggplot2)
library(magick)

legend_plot <- ggplot(data.frame(x = seq(17, 30, length.out = 256),
                                 y = 1),
                      aes(x = x, y = y, fill = x)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#313695", "#74add1", "#ffffbf", "#f46d43", "#a50026")
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(17, 20, 23, 26, 30),
                     labels = c("17°C", "20°C", "23°C", "26°C", "30°C"),
                     position = "bottom") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks.x = element_line(),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

ggsave("legend.png", legend_plot, width = 4, height = 0.6, dpi = 150)


scene <- image_read("scene.png")
legend <- image_read("legend.png")
legend <- image_resize(legend, geometry_size_pixels(width = 400))

final <- image_composite(scene, legend, 
                         offset = "+50+700", gravity = "southwest")
image_write(final, "final_map.png")

Q: Choosing the best AI coding assistant for reasoning vs speed vs workflow efficiency A:

You have to decide which of the tradeoffs you find least problematic, then. If you want more reasoning then it's likely to take longer, for example - that should not be particularly surprising.

Your described wishlist is pretty generic so I'm not sure we've really got enough info to give you meaningful guidance about which way to turn.

I do agree though that you need to largely ignore the hype, and decide what you are going to use AI for in your workflow, and then experiment with which tool or tools seems to be good at those particular tasks.

Q: Variable propagation between Yocto recipes - Best practices A:

If you just want to have a variable to control the type of compilation of some recipe, then it is not done like what you described (using two other image recipes).

Keep in mind that variables defined in a recipe are not visible in other recipes. If you want a variable to be global for all recipes then put it in a .conf file such as local.conf.

About what you said:

the problem in my opinion is that the app.bb is parsed and compiled first ( VAR not assigned yet )then the image-a.bb is parsed at the end .

That is not true even if images are parsed first (for the reason I explained above).

That being said, I am not sure if what you want to accomplish is reasonable. So, you want that VAR1 gets a value when you build image-a so that app gets compiled in different way, and same for image-b. That's not how things can be done in Yocto (or thought about in my opinion).

I don't understand why you tie the app recipe with the image you are building. In Yocto you cannot simply change the behavior of do_compile of a recipe from the context of other recipe (in your case image-a and image-b) unless you find a way to extend the app recipe itself automatically with BBCLASSEXTEND and create a class that changes the variable you want. Like you set VAR1 to value-a as default value in app and then do something like:

VAR1 ?= "value-a"
VAR1:class-image-b-way = "value-b"
BBCLASSEXTEND += "image-b-way"

and then in a image-b-way.bbclass you add class-image-b-way to OVERRIDES . Doing this you can now set app to IMAGE_INSTALL of image-a and set app-image-b-way to IMAGE_INSTALL of image-b. This way BitBake will autoamtically extend the app recipe for you and change VAR1. This may seem easy to implement but it will create two different workding directories for app recipe and this seems overengineering.

For me, what blocking me is that you have two images and both images are adding the same recipe name and you want to build the recipe differently for each image, this is itself is the idea that sounds not logical to me that I cannot think of a solution other than extending the app recipe as I explained.

If I would have one image or multiple images, I don't tie the app recipe to the image name, I just define a new override and use it inside the app recipe, like I define (in local.conf or better in the custom distro of the project):

DISTROOVERRIDES .= "${@bb.utils.contains('TARGET_NAME', 'b', ':way-b', '', d)"

and in app.bb:

VAR1 = "value-a"
VAR1:way-b = "value-b"

Now you can keep TARGET_NAME undefined so way-b will not end up in OVERRIDES and VAR1 will take value-a. Otherwise you define it in local.conf to b and it will make VAR1 take value-b by force of override. And now you can of course add TARGET_NAME to BB_ENV_PASSTHROUGH so you can pass it from your shell environment to make it easier:

$ bitbake core-image-minimal # <== builds with "value-a"
$ TARGET_NAME=b bitbake core-image-minimal # <== builds with "value-b"

Again, you cannot change a variable of a recipe from another recipe. So the real question is why you want to compile app based on the image name itself, my opinion is that should not be tied together, just control how app is compiled with a solution like I described, for example:

$ bitbake image-a # <== this will simply add `app` by default with `value-a`
$ TARGET_NAME=b bitbake image-b # <== this will build app with value-b

That should do it for you, and keep in mind that you can also do:

$ TARGET_NAME=b bitbake image-a # <== this will build app with value-b

There are more solutions but they are really really overengineering and complex that I won't bother mentioning them.

Q: SQL Select WHERE duplicate in one column x AND column y != z A:

None of the above will work if you can have a unique column in table to identify which one to keep. In case of true duplicate, you will need to 1. extract duplecate records to a temp table 2. delete all duplicate rows and 3. add de-duped records as follows insert into table select distinct * from temp table
